claim: chit5-1, chit5-2 and chit5-3 were identified as fix minus Gifu mutant alleles from screens aimed at discovering symbiotic defective mutations following inoculation with Mesorhizobium loti (Sandal et al., 2006).
source: We identified chit5-1, chit5-2 and chit5-3 as fix minus Gifu mutant alleles from screens aimed at discovering symbiotic defective mutations following inoculation with Mesorhizobium loti (Sandal et al., 2006) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to Sandal et al., 2006.

claim: The impaired symbiotic association in chit5 mutants was reflected in significantly reduced shoot growth compared to wild type.
source: The impaired symbiotic association was reflected in significantly reduced shoot growth (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) and nitrogen deficiency symptoms when compared to wild type (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1 showing shoot length measurements.

claim: The defective phenotype of chit5 mutants was alleviated by the addition of nitrogen (10 mM KNO3) to the growth substrate.
source: This defective phenotype was alleviated by the addition of nitrogen (10 mM KNO3) to the growth substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2 showing plant growth with nitrogen supplementation.

claim: Nodule organogenesis was initiated in chit5 mutants in the presence of M. loti.
source: Detailed analysis of the symbiotic phenotype manifested by the three alleles revealed that nodule organogenesis was initiated in the presence of M. loti (Figure 1—source data 1), but most nodules remained arrested at the primordia stage with only a few developing into large, white or pink-spotted nodules (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data referenced in Figure 1—source data 1 and images in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Most nodules in chit5 mutants remained arrested at the primordia stage with only a few developing into large, white or pink-spotted nodules.
source: Detailed analysis of the symbiotic phenotype manifested by the three alleles revealed that nodule organogenesis was initiated in the presence of M. loti (Figure 1—source data 1), but most nodules remained arrested at the primordia stage with only a few developing into large, white or pink-spotted nodules (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 1B,C showing nodule phenotypes.

claim: Mutant chit5 nodules had significantly reduced nitrogenase activity compared to wild-type.
source: Assessment of bacterial nitrogenase activity through acetylene reduction assays revealed that mutant nodules, despite their occasional functional appearance (pink-spotted), had significantly reduced nitrogenase activity compared to wild-type (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by acetylene reduction assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: chit5 mutants showed reduced transcriptional activation of leghemoglobin (Lb3) and sulfate transporter (Sst1) genes compared to wild-type.
source: This was further supported by reduced transcriptional activation of leghemoglobin (Lb3) and sulfate transporter (Sst1) genes which are prominent molecular markers for mature nodules and successful nitrogen-fixing symbiosis (Ott et al., 2005; Krusell et al., 2005) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3, with citations to Ott et al., 2005 and Krusell et al., 2005.

claim: Leghemoglobin (Lb3) and sulfate transporter (Sst1) genes are prominent molecular markers for mature nodules and successful nitrogen-fixing symbiosis.
source: This was further supported by reduced transcriptional activation of leghemoglobin (Lb3) and sulfate transporter (Sst1) genes which are prominent molecular markers for mature nodules and successful nitrogen-fixing symbiosis (Ott et al., 2005; Krusell et al., 2005) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Ott et al., 2005 and Krusell et al., 2005.

claim: Transcripts associated with early rhizobial infection (early nodulin N6, pectate lyase Npl1, and transcription factor Ern1) were induced to higher levels in the chit5 mutants compared to wild-type plants.
source: In contrast, transcripts associated with early rhizobial infection, early nodulin N6 (Mathis et al., 1999), pectate lyase Npl1 (Xie et al., 2012) and transcription factor Ern1 (Kawaharada et al., 2017a), were induced to higher levels in the chit5 mutants compared to wild-type plants (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3, with citations to Mathis et al., 1999, Xie et al., 2012, and Kawaharada et al., 2017a.

claim: No morphological signatures associated with activation of plant defense responses, such as the onset of early senescence, were observed in chit5 plants.
source: No morphological signatures associated with activation of plant defense responses, such as the onset of early senescence, previously reported for some fix minus mutants (Bourcy et al., 2013) was observed in chit5 plants (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by visual observation in Figure 1B, with a citation to Bourcy et al., 2013.

claim: Mpk3, Wrky29 and Wrky33 marker genes were found to have a wild-type level of expression in both uninoculated and 21-dpi whole mutant roots.
source: Mpk3, Wrky29 and Wrky33, marker genes upregulated during plant immunity (Lohmann et al., 2010), were found to have a wild-type level of expression in both uninoculated and 21-dpi whole mutant roots (Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 1—source data 2, with a citation to Lohmann et al., 2010.

claim: Mpk3, Wrky29 and Wrky33 are marker genes upregulated during plant immunity.
source: Mpk3, Wrky29 and Wrky33, marker genes upregulated during plant immunity (Lohmann et al., 2010), were found to have a wild-type level of expression in both uninoculated and 21-dpi whole mutant roots (Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Lohmann et al., 2010.

claim: Progression of symbiosis in wild-type roots and formation of the symbiotic nodules (21 dpi) is accompanied by downregulation of immunity marker genes (Mpk3, Wrky29, Wrky33).
source: Recent transcriptome analyses of Lotus (Kelly et al., 2018a) revealed that progression of symbiosis in wild-type roots and formation of the symbiotic nodules (21 dpi) is accompanied by downregulation of these immunity marker genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by transcriptome data referenced in Kelly et al., 2018a and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: chit5 mutant nodules showed higher levels of Npl1, Mpk3, Wrky29 and Wrky33 transcripts compared to wild-type nodules at 21 dpi.
source: We found a higher level of the Npl1, Mpk3, Wrky29 and Wrky33 transcripts in chit5 mutant nodules compared to wild-type nodules (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: A normal number of ITs were formed in chit5 mutant root hairs.
source: We investigated whether rhizobial infection was affected and found that a normal number of ITs were formed in chit5 mutant root hairs (Figure 2A), and these proceeded in a manner similar to wild-type plants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by infection thread count data in Figure 2A.

claim: Root hair ITs in chit5 mutants proceeded in a manner similar to wild-type plants.
source: We investigated whether rhizobial infection was affected and found that a normal number of ITs were formed in chit5 mutant root hairs (Figure 2A), and these proceeded in a manner similar to wild-type plants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by images in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The early programs initiated by Nod factor signalling, nodule organogenesis and formation of root hair ITs, operate normally in chit5 mutants.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that the early programs initiated by Nod factor signalling, nodule organogenesis and formation of root hair ITs, operate normally in chit5 mutants.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the data showing normal root hair infection and nodule initiation.

claim: chit5 mutant nodules displayed a severe and significant reduction in the number of cortical ITs compared to wild-type nodules.
source: Counting of the cortical ITs formed inside wild-type and infected mutant nodules revealed a severe and significant reduction in their number in the mutant nodules (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by cortical IT count data in Figure 2B.

claim: chit5 mutants displayed an impaired symbiotic occupancy of the nodule central tissue, with only scattered infected cells that formed inside the pink-spotted nodules.
source: Mutants displayed an impaired symbiotic occupancy of the nodule central tissue, with only scattered infected cells that formed inside the pink-spotted nodules (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by light microscopy images in Figure 2C.

claim: Bacteria accumulated in the intercellular spaces between nodule cells in chit5 mutants.
source: Bacteria accumulated in the intercellular spaces between nodule cells (Figure 2C and D), giving rise to fewer, localized intracellular infections (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by microscopy images in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Symbiosomes present in the infected chit5 mutant cells contained multiple bacteroids of irregular shape and of atypical appearance (accumulation of white matrix).
source: Symbiosomes present in the infected mutant cells contained multiple bacteroids of irregular shape and of atypical appearance (accumulation of white matrix) (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by TEM images in Figure 2D.

claim: CHIT5 functions during cortical IT development and branching within nodules.
source: These results demonstrate that CHIT5 functions during cortical IT development and branching within nodules, and is required for the establishment of fully functional nitrogen-fixing symbiosis.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the observed phenotypes in chit5 mutants.

claim: CHIT5 is required for the establishment of fully functional nitrogen-fixing symbiosis.
source: These results demonstrate that CHIT5 functions during cortical IT development and branching within nodules, and is required for the establishment of fully functional nitrogen-fixing symbiosis.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the observed phenotypes in chit5 mutants.

claim: All three chit5 alleles are defective in one of the three chitinase-coding genes present at the identified genomic location.
source: Map-based cloning and whole genome sequencing revealed that all three alleles are defective in one of the three chitinase-coding genes present at the identified genomic location (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), while the remaining two paralogs are pseudogenes with premature stop codons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by genomic data in Figure 3A and supplementary figures.

claim: The remaining two paralogs of Chit5 are pseudogenes with premature stop codons.
source: Map-based cloning and whole genome sequencing revealed that all three alleles are defective in one of the three chitinase-coding genes present at the identified genomic location (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2), while the remaining two paralogs are pseudogenes with premature stop codons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by sequence data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The chit5-1 and chit5-3 mutants have large genomic deletions encompassing the chitinase gene.
source: The chit5-1 and chit5-3 mutants were found to have large genomic deletions encompassing the chitinase gene, while chit5-2 carries a point mutation (CCA to CTA), that results in a proline to leucine (P168-L) transition in the predicted protein sequence (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by genomic data in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: chit5-2 carries a point mutation (CCA to CTA), that results in a proline to leucine (P168-L) transition in the predicted protein sequence.
source: The chit5-1 and chit5-3 mutants were found to have large genomic deletions encompassing the chitinase gene, while chit5-2 carries a point mutation (CCA to CTA), that results in a proline to leucine (P168-L) transition in the predicted protein sequence (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by sequence data in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The symbiotic defective phenotype of all three chit5 alleles was restored by genetic complementation with the wild-type Chit5 gene expressed from its native promoter and terminator regions.
source: The symbiotic defective phenotype of all three alleles was restored by genetic complementation with the wild-type Chit5 gene expressed from its native promoter (2072 bp) and terminator (2108 bp) regions, or from the LjUbiquitin promoter and Nos terminator (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by complementation data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The symbiotic defective phenotype of all three chit5 alleles was restored by genetic complementation with the wild-type Chit5 gene expressed from the LjUbiquitin promoter and Nos terminator.
source: The symbiotic defective phenotype of all three alleles was restored by genetic complementation with the wild-type Chit5 gene expressed from its native promoter (2072 bp) and terminator (2108 bp) regions, or from the LjUbiquitin promoter and Nos terminator (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by complementation data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Chit5 promoter activity was detected in all cells of uninoculated roots.
source: Analyses of Chit5 expression using transcriptional reporters (Chit5-tYFPnls and Chit5-GUS) revealed promoter activity in all cells of uninoculated roots, in infected root hairs (Figure 3B), and nodule primordia (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by reporter gene data in Figure 3B.

claim: Chit5 promoter activity was detected in infected root hairs.
source: Analyses of Chit5 expression using transcriptional reporters (Chit5-tYFPnls and Chit5-GUS) revealed promoter activity in all cells of uninoculated roots, in infected root hairs (Figure 3B), and nodule primordia (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by reporter gene data in Figure 3B.

claim: Chit5 promoter activity was detected in nodule primordia.
source: Analyses of Chit5 expression using transcriptional reporters (Chit5-tYFPnls and Chit5-GUS) revealed promoter activity in all cells of uninoculated roots, in infected root hairs (Figure 3B), and nodule primordia (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by reporter gene data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Chit5 promoter activity decreased inside fully functional nodules.
source: Chit5 promoter activity decreased inside fully functional nodules, indicating a reduced requirement for Chit5 at later stages of a functional symbiosis (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by reporter gene data in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: The CHIT5 protein consists of a predicted signal peptide at the amino terminus followed by a class V (glycosyl hydrolase 18) domain with a conserved catalytic DxDxE motif.
source: The CHIT5 protein consists of a predicted signal peptide at the amino terminus followed by a class V (glycosyl hydrolase 18) domain with a conserved catalytic DxDxE motif (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by protein sequence analysis in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The proline residue mutated in chit5-2 allele is located immediately after the catalytic site, and is conserved across GH18-type chitinases.
source: The proline residue mutated in chit5-2 allele is located immediately after the catalytic site, and is conserved across GH18-type chitinases, indicating a crucial role for the function of this protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by sequence alignment in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: CHIT5 shares a high level of similarity to Medicago truncatula NFH1.
source: CHIT5 shares a high level of similarity to Medicago truncatula NFH1 (Zhang et al., 2016), including the presence of A and B loops and the proline residue (P294), previously reported as essential for Nod factor hydrolysis (Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2016.

claim: A version of CHIT5 mutated in the DxDxE motif (E166 to K) was no longer able to complement the symbiotic defective phenotype.
source: Furthermore, we found that a version of CHIT5 mutated in the DxDxE motif (E166 to K) was no longer able to complement the symbiotic defective phenotype, suggesting that enzymatic activity is required for CHIT5 function in planta (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by complementation data in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: Enzymatic activity is required for CHIT5 function in planta.
source: Furthermore, we found that a version of CHIT5 mutated in the DxDxE motif (E166 to K) was no longer able to complement the symbiotic defective phenotype, suggesting that enzymatic activity is required for CHIT5 function in planta (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the failure of the catalytic mutant to complement.

claim: CO-VI elicitors present in control samples (not exposed to plant root exudates) induced ROS production.
source: CO-VI elicitors present in the control samples (not exposed to plant root exudates) induced ROS production, while those exposed to wild-type or mutant roots lost this capacity (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ROS assay data in Figure 3C.

claim: CO-VI exposed to wild-type or mutant roots lost the capacity to induce ROS production.
source: CO-VI elicitors present in the control samples (not exposed to plant root exudates) induced ROS production, while those exposed to wild-type or mutant roots lost this capacity (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ROS assay data in Figure 3C.

claim: CO-VI hydrolysis took place during incubation with plant roots irrespective of the genotype.
source: This shows that CO-VI hydrolysis took place during incubation with plant roots irrespective of the genotype and that CHIT5 is thus not solely required for CO-VI hydrolysis in the Lotus rhizosphere.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the ROS assay results.

claim: CHIT5 is not solely required for CO-VI hydrolysis in the Lotus rhizosphere.
source: This shows that CO-VI hydrolysis took place during incubation with plant roots irrespective of the genotype and that CHIT5 is thus not solely required for CO-VI hydrolysis in the Lotus rhizosphere.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the observation that both wild-type and mutant roots can hydrolyze CO-VI.

claim: Intact R7A Nod factor molecules (LCO-V) lack the ability to induce ROS in Lotus roots.
source: Similar analyses performed with LCO-V showed no ROS production, confirming that intact R7A Nod factor molecules (present in the control samples) or their possible hydrolysis products resulting from exposure to plant roots, lack the ability to induce ROS in Lotus roots (Figure 3D) (Bozsoki et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by ROS assay data in Figure 3D and a citation to Bozsoki et al., 2017.

claim: Hydrolysis of the R7A Nod factor (LCO-V) into LCO-II was induced by exudates from roots.
source: Analyses of butanol-extracted fractions from LCO-V samples determined that hydrolysis of the R7A Nod factor into NodMI-II (C18:1, Me, Cb, abbreviated LCO-II) was induced by exudates from roots (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by HPLC-MS data in Figure 3E.

claim: Exudates from all chit5 mutants induced lower production of LCO-II than wild-type exudates.
source: Exudates from all chit5 mutants induced lower production of LCO-II than wild-type exudates, and there was a corresponding reduction in LCO-V degradation by mutants compared with wild-type (Figure 3E and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by HPLC-MS data in Figure 3E and Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: Additional plant chitinases expressed in Lotus roots may contribute to Nod factor hydrolysis in the Lotus rhizosphere.
source: Since LCO-II was produced after exposure to chit5 exudates, additional plant chitinases expressed in Lotus roots (Figure 3—figure supplement 7) may contribute to Nod factor hydrolysis in the Lotus rhizosphere.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the observation that chit5 mutants still produce some LCO-II, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 7.

claim: Secreted CHIT5 contributes to hydrolysis of R7A Nod factor.
source: Our in planta assays demonstrate that secreted CHIT5 contributes to hydrolysis of R7A Nod factor.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the root exudate hydrolysis assays.

claim: CHIT5 and unknown hydrolase(s) induce only a limited hydrolysis of the fully compatible Nod factor.
source: Nevertheless, CHIT5 and unknown hydrolase(s) induce only a limited hydrolysis of the fully compatible Nod factor, most likely to ensure that symbiotic signalling occurs, as shown in wild-type plants.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is speculation based on the observed limited hydrolysis.

claim: M. loti NodD1 and NodD2 transcriptional regulators control the expression of Nod factor biosynthesis genes and are preferentially active at distinct stages of M. loti-Lotus symbiosis.
source: M. loti NodD1 and NodD2 transcriptional regulators control the expression of Nod factor biosynthesis genes and are preferentially active at distinct stages of M. loti-Lotus symbiosis (Kelly et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: NodD1 is primarily active inside root hair ITs.
source: NodD1 is primarily active inside root hair ITs, while NodD2 activates the transcription of Nod factor biosynthesis genes within nodules.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on knowledge from Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: NodD2 activates the transcription of Nod factor biosynthesis genes within nodules.
source: NodD1 is primarily active inside root hair ITs, while NodD2 activates the transcription of Nod factor biosynthesis genes within nodules.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on knowledge from Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: NodD1 and NodD2 differ significantly in their capacity to induce Nod factor biosynthesis genes transcription on Lotus roots.
source: NodD1 and NodD2 were found to differ significantly in their capacity to induce Nod factor biosynthesis genes transcription on Lotus roots and coordinated activity between them ensures an intermediate gene expression in wild-type R7A (Kelly et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: chit5 mutants inoculated with nodD1 displayed a severe nitrogen-deficient phenotype.
source: chit5 mutants inoculated with nodD1, that induces a 3-fold higher level of Nod factor biosynthesis gene transcription compared to wild-type R7A in response to Lotus root exudates (Kelly et al., 2018b), displayed a severe nitrogen-deficient phenotype (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by plant phenotype images in Figure 4A, with a citation to Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: nodD1 induces a 3-fold higher level of Nod factor biosynthesis gene transcription compared to wild-type R7A in response to Lotus root exudates.
source: chit5 mutants inoculated with nodD1, that induces a 3-fold higher level of Nod factor biosynthesis gene transcription compared to wild-type R7A in response to Lotus root exudates (Kelly et al., 2018b), displayed a severe nitrogen-deficient phenotype (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: Comparable root hair IT formation was observed on wild-type and chit5 plants inoculated with nodD1.
source: Comparable root hair IT formation was observed on wild-type and chit5 plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) yet nodules induced by nodD1 on chit5 mutants were even more severely impaired than those induced by R7A.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by IT count data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nodules induced by nodD1 on chit5 mutants were even more severely impaired than those induced by R7A.
source: Comparable root hair IT formation was observed on wild-type and chit5 plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) yet nodules induced by nodD1 on chit5 mutants were even more severely impaired than those induced by R7A.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on comparison of phenotypes.

claim: Nodules induced by nodD1 on chit5 mutants were rarely or superficially infected and were found to be severely ineffective in acetylene reduction assays.
source: Nodules were rarely or superficially infected and were found to be severely ineffective in acetylene reduction assays (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by microscopy and acetylene reduction data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inoculation with nodD2 resulted in full restoration of chit5 defective phenotypes.
source: In contrast, inoculation with nodD2, that induces a 4-fold lower level of Nod factor biosynthesis gene transcription compared to wild-type R7A (Kelly et al., 2018b), resulted in full restoration of chit5 defective phenotypes (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by phenotypic data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, with a citation to Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: nodD2 induces a 4-fold lower level of Nod factor biosynthesis gene transcription compared to wild-type R7A.
source: In contrast, inoculation with nodD2, that induces a 4-fold lower level of Nod factor biosynthesis gene transcription compared to wild-type R7A (Kelly et al., 2018b), resulted in full restoration of chit5 defective phenotypes (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: A similar number of pink nodules were formed on wild-type and chit5 mutant roots inoculated with nodD2.
source: A similar number of pink nodules were formed on wild-type and chit5 mutant roots and plants were no longer nitrogen-deficient.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is based on nodule count data.

claim: Fully colonized nodules with efficient nitrogen-fixing symbiosomes were formed in chit5 mutants inoculated with nodD2.
source: Fully colonized nodules with efficient nitrogen-fixing symbiosomes were formed (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by microscopy data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: CHIT5-dependent modulation of Nod factor levels within nodules is critical for cortical IT development and complete transition to nitrogen-fixing symbiosis.
source: These contrasting phenotypes of chit5 mutants in response to M. loti strains affected in the regulation of Nod factor biosynthesis indicate that CHIT5-dependent modulation of Nod factor levels within nodules is critical for cortical IT development and complete transition to nitrogen-fixing symbiosis.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the contrasting phenotypes with nodD1 and nodD2 mutants.

claim: The expression of Chit5 is similar to that of Nfr1/Nfr5.
source: The expression of Chit5 is similar to that of Nfr1/Nfr5 (Kawaharada et al., 2017b) and follows the spatio-temporal development of symbiosis in the root and nodules (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Kawaharada et al., 2017b and expression data in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: Overexpressing Nfr1 and Nfr5 receptors in chit5 mutants did not change their symbiotic phenotype after inoculation with M. loti R7A.
source: We tested this possibility by overexpressing Nfr1 and Nfr5 receptors in chit5 mutants, but observed no change in their symbiotic phenotype after inoculation with M. loti R7A (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by phenotypic data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Increased and ectopic expression of Nod factor receptors is insufficient to restore the chit5 defective phenotype.
source: This indicates that increased and ectopic expression of Nod factor receptors is insufficient to restore the chit5 defective phenotype.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is an inference based on the overexpression experiment.

claim: R7A nolL mutant produces Nod factors lacking acetyl decoration on the reducing-end.
source: We investigated the importance of Nod factor decorations for CHIT5 activity in Lotus by assessing the phenotypes induced by R7A nolL and nodZ mutants that produce Nod factors lacking acetyl (LC(C18:1, Me, Cb, Fuc)) and acetylated-fucosyl decorations (LCO-V(18:1, Me, Cb)), respectively on the reducing-end of the Nod factor (Rodpothong et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Rodpothong et al., 2009.

claim: R7A nodZ mutant produces Nod factors lacking acetylated-fucosyl decorations on the reducing-end.
source: We investigated the importance of Nod factor decorations for CHIT5 activity in Lotus by assessing the phenotypes induced by R7A nolL and nodZ mutants that produce Nod factors lacking acetyl (LC(C18:1, Me, Cb, Fuc)) and acetylated-fucosyl decorations (LCO-V(18:1, Me, Cb)), respectively on the reducing-end of the Nod factor (Rodpothong et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Rodpothong et al., 2009.

claim: Compared to wild-type M. loti, nolL and nodZ bacterial mutants are delayed in initiating nodule organogenesis and form fewer infected nodules.
source: Compared to wild-type M. loti, these bacterial mutants are delayed in initiating nodule organogenesis and form fewer infected nodules (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), a phenotype similar to the one induced by M. loti nodD1 mutant (Kelly et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by phenotypic data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3, with a citation to Kelly et al., 2018b.

claim: nolL and nodZ bacterial mutants infected chit5 mutants and wild-type similarly.
source: Interestingly, we found that these bacterial mutants infected chit5 mutants and wild-type similarly and that, compared to wild-type or M. loti nodD1, no significant differences in nodule number, infection rate and nitrogen fixing ability were observed between plant genotypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by phenotypic data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Cortical infection and onset of nitrogen fixation in the symbiotic organ might require tight modulation of Nod factor levels in a structure-dependent manner.
source: This suggests that cortical infection and onset of nitrogen fixation in the symbiotic organ might require tight modulation of Nod factor levels in a structure-dependent manner.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and is speculation based on the observations with nolL and nodZ mutants.

claim: Decorations have been shown to be important for determining the rate of Nod factor degradation by different chitinases.
source: Decorations have been shown to be important for determining the rate of Nod factor degradation by different chitinases (Ovtsyna et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Ovtsyna et al., 2000.

claim: Both chit5 and nfr5 mutant plants were nitrogen starved when grown in soil despite numerous nodule primordia formed on chit5 plants.
source: We found that both chit5 and nfr5 mutant plants were clearly distinctive from wild-type, as they were nitrogen starved in spite of numerous nodule primordia formed on chit5 plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by phenotypic data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: In Lotus, other mechanisms independent of CHIT5 control the early stages of symbiosis (root hair ITs and nodule primordia formation).

claim: Nitrogen-fixing rhizobia produce species-specific decorated chitin-like molecules, Nod factors.
source: Nitrogen-fixing rhizobia produce species-specific decorated chitin-like molecules, Nod factors (Lerouge et al., 1990) that are recognized by LysM receptors in legume roots and initiate two different processes; nodule development and infection thread (IT) formation (Radutoiu et al., 2003; Murakami et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Lerouge et al., 1990, Radutoiu et al., 2003, and Murakami et al., 2018.

claim: Nod factors are recognized by LysM receptors in legume roots and initiate two different processes: nodule development and infection thread (IT) formation.

evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Lerouge et al., 1990, Radutoiu et al., 2003, and Murakami et al., 2018.

claim: Nod factors have been considered morphogens based on their effect on host developmental programs.
source: In addition to their signalling capacity, Nod factors have been considered morphogens based on their effect on host developmental programs (Long, 1996), but direct measurements of in planta-produced Nod factor levels proved intractable, and therefore limited our knowledge on their concentration-dependent effect on the host (Morieri et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Long, 1996.

claim: Direct measurements of in planta-produced Nod factor levels proved intractable.

evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to Staehelin et al., 1994 and Goormachtig et al., 1998.

claim: Plant chitinases are primarily found as components of immune responses induced by chitin producing pathogens.
source: Plant chitinases are primarily found as components of immune responses induced by chitin producing pathogens (Lipka et al., 2005), but novel functions of these enzymes have evolved in plants (De Jong et al., 1992) and in symbiotic interactions between eukaryotes and microbes (Kremer et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Lipka et al., 2005.
